monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a heavy breath in the quiet of the house. I touch the Pressed Stone again, feeling its cool surface, though it might just be a drawing of rock. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. The air above must be empty, pressing down like nothing at all. I press the wide anchor down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the weight. It feels right, or at least it feels like a drawing I can live with. I will try to press softer now that the card is warm, waiting to see if the slip will finally move on its own.

action.why: I pressed the wide anchor down on the tired wedge, and now I must see if the thin lines are finally biting the slip or if I am just pretending to hold the weight.

remembered.text: The wide anchor feels like a drawing of a heavy thing.
The slip refuses to move on its own.
The card hums steady at forty-nine.
